topic: Control features - what verified control tools existed, when, and in which product (image-to-video, first/last frame, camera control, references, editing, native audio, multi-shot, extend, 4K)
method_notes: All pages were fetched from the Higgsfield sandbox (open internet) and every quote was checked programmatically against the fetched page text (whitespace-normalised, HTML entities decoded, curly quotes straightened) before being written. Wayback Machine captures are cited with the http:// form (the https form was intermittently failing) and the exact capture timestamp in the URL. Kling, Barchart and the Luma changelog are JavaScript-rendered and were read with a headless browser (Playwright). A few quotes live in markup (page metadata such as datePublished, or a Hugging Face raw README) and were checked against raw HTML. The Runway Director Mode date is decoded from the LinkedIn activity ID. Dates are first-verified dates from primary sources; secondary reports are only used where labelled secondary. The matrix is facts only: no scores.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: Sora 2 did not introduce native audio. Veo 3 generated video with audio on 2025-05-20, four months before Sora 2 (2025-09-30). Earlier audio work was research (MM-Diffusion, 2022) or add-on audio (Google V2A 2024, Meta Movie Gen audio 2024).

Camera control did not begin with Runway Gen-3 (2024) or Veo/Flow (2025). Runway said Director Mode was "available now in Gen-2" on 2023-09-13 (LinkedIn post, date decoded from its ID) and shipped Motion Brush on 2023-11-23. Open research such as AnimateDiff MotionLoRA (2023-09) and MotionCtrl (2023-12-06) also came first.

Runway Gen-4 did not invent reference-based character consistency. Vidu Subject to Video (2024-09-11), Vidu 1.5 (2024-11-13), Pika 2.0 Scene Ingredients (Dec 2024), MiniMax S2V-01 (2025-01-10) and Kling Elements (2025-01-23) came first; Runway References shipped 2025-04-30 after the 2025-03-31 Gen-4 announcement.

Veo 3.1 (2025-10-15) did not introduce Ingredients, Frames to Video or Extend. Google's own post says it brought audio to "existing capabilities"; Flow launched with camera controls, Scenebuilder and ingredients on 2025-05-20.

First/last-frame control predates Veo 3.1 and Luma Ray3 Modify. Luma's API page advertised start and end keyframes by 2024-09-16 (a secondary report says 2024-06-27), Runway added last frame on 2024-08-05, and Pika launched Pikaframes on 2025-02-27. Ray3 Modify (2025-12-18) added start/end control to video-to-video for the first time.

Gen-2 was not publicly available in March 2023. 2023-03-20 was an announcement; Runway's own interview dates the introduction of Gen-2 to June 2023, and image-to-video from arbitrary starting frames was a later update (by 2023-09-28).

Google's 4K is upscaling, not native generation: Veo 3.1 (2026-01-13) and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash (2026-08-27) both describe 1080p/4K that way (the Gemini API docs list 4k as an output size). Kling calls its 2026-04-23 4K mode native and "world's first", but LTX-2 claimed native 4K on 2025-10-23; the earliest verified 4K upscale is Runway Gen-3 Alpha (2025-01-10).

Kling's June 2025 "sound integrated" change was not native audio. Its release history logs AI sound generation from video on 2025-03-27 and integrated sound on 2025-06-26, and reserves "Native Audio" for Kling 2.6 (2025-12-03).

Multi-shot is not a 2026 invention. Sora's Feb 2024 page claimed multiple shots, Amazon Nova Reel 1.1 shipped two-minute multi-shot videos on 2025-04-07 (chained 6-second shots), Seedance 1.0 (2025-06-10) called it native, and Kling 3.0 added Multi-Shot on 2026-01-31.

Sora's control features (cameos, characters, storyboards, extensions, editor) can no longer be used: the Sora web and app closed on 2026-04-26 and the Sora 2 API shut down on 2026-09-24 with no one-to-one replacement API.
Kling 4.0 is not yet publicly launched. On 2026-09-28 Kling opened Kling 4.0 Flash to a limited group for early access and says the full Kling 4.0 launches in October.

Longer clips come from chaining, not one long take: Veo 3.1 reaches 148 seconds by extending Veo-generated video in 7-second steps, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash reaches 40 seconds in 10-second steps, and Nova Reel's two minutes are 6-second shots.

Motion Brush did not originate at Kling. Runway shipped Motion Brush on 2023-11-23 and Multi-Motion Brush on 2024-01-18; Kling 1.5's Motion Brush (up to six elements) appears in a press release dated 2024-11-28.
Runway Aleph was not the first video-to-video editor: Runway Gen-1 (2023-02-06), Gen-3 Alpha Video to Video (2024-09-13) and Luma Modify Video (2025-06-02) all came before Aleph (2025-07-25).
